additionalCoursework: The Committee on Admissions looks favorably on a program of study that includes at least one year of college mathematics and advanced science subjects. Courses in biochemistry, biostatistics and statistics are strongly recommended. Other desirable courses include anatomy, physiology, histology, cell biology, genetics, neuroscience, social sciences, humanities, sociology and psychology.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: SUNY Downstate is committed to maintaining a diverse and inclusive environment where all students can thrive academically and achieve their personal best. We embrace a broad view of diversity that is not limited to, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, ability, language, culture, religious practices, socioeconomic background, and life experiences. The Office of Diversity Education and Research provides an array of services: Oversee undergraduate pipelines programs;  Facilitate student-led peer mentorship programs; counseling to students interested in diversity programs; information on diversity scholarships for matriculating students; support to student diversity groups; opportunities for community engagement and outreach; integrate lectures on cultural competency and social determinants into the curriculum; networking events; academic counseling to current students; Link students to opportunities in health disparities and health equity research.

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At SUNY Downstate, you'll learn your craft in one of the world's most diverse communities.

Every program at SUNY Downstate has close ties to the Flatbush community. That means you'll see firsthand how equitable health care can change the world. Downstate is home to more than 100 volunteer service projects. Each provides rich opportunities for faculty, staff and students to connect with others.

Because our expertise is so wide-ranging, we draw from a deep well of talent when we confront community challenges. For example, the student-run Brooklyn Free Clinic brings together volunteers from our College of Medicine, School of Health Professions, College of Nursing, and School of Public Health to conduct health screenings and provide care. In the Downstate Dialysis Sidekicks Program, students keep company with young patients as they endure the day-long procedure. And as we mentor high school students we bring together students in every discipline, proving STEM careers are within reach.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The primary goal of the College of Medicine is to graduate excellent physicians. Whether the student's ultimate goal is general or specialty practice, research, medical administration or academic medicine, the College provides a comprehensive educational experience for all students.

For more information see https://www.downstate.edu/education-training/college-of-medicine/curriculum/index.html

The educational objectives of the curriculum are intended to provide students with the basics that they will need to embark upon graduate medical education in the field of their choice, and ultimately to become competent and compassionate physicians. To achieve these objectives, the College has set standards of knowledge and develops the skills and attitudes necessary to enable students to reach their goals.

The Integrated Pathways Curriculum emphasizes learning across disciplines with an emphasis on understanding core principles.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
All letters (packet or individual) must be submitted on letterhead, and must be signed by the letter writer. Letters not meeting these requirements will not be considered. All letters must be submitted electronically—through the AMCAS letter service (including Virtual Evals or Interfolio). The AMCAS application letter types are: Committee letter, Letter packet or Individual Letter. We do not accept letters of recommendation sent by mail, email, or fax.

If you are submitting an AMCAS Committee Letter or a Letter Packet, we accept all the letters included in the packet. At least one of the letter should be from a science professor who has taught you in a biology, chemistry or physics course.

Visit website for additional information: https://www.downstate.edu/education-training/college-of-medicine/admissions/letters-of-recommendation.html
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
**Response to COVID-19 - Information for 2026 Admissions Cycle**

We understand that the COVID-19 pandemic may have impacted different facets of an applicant's portfolio, including, but not limited to: Pass/Fail grades, on-line coursework, and/or discontinuation of activities. The Admissions Committee will be flexible in its admission criteria and will continue to holistically review and evaluate each application.  We ask only that you provide a letter or document confirming the reason you opted for these different experiences. 

The Committee on Admissions considers the total qualifications of each applicant without regard to sex, race, color, creed, national origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, marital status, or disability. Decisions regarding admission are based on multiple factors including prior academic performance; completion of the courses required for admission; the potential for academic success including performance on standardized tests such as the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT); communication skills, character, personal skills, health-related experiences, and motivation for a career in medicine. Admissions preference is given to USA citizens and permanent residents who are New York State residents, although well-qualified out of state applicants are also accepted. We welcome and encourage applications from women and members of groups underrepresented in medicine. 

Visit website for additional information https://www.downstate.edu/education-training/college-of-medicine/admissions/policies/index.html

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The College of Medicine strives to select students who possess the intelligence, integrity and personal and emotional characteristics that are considered necessary to become an effective health professional.  Students admitted to the College of Medicine should have the intellectual and physical abilities to acquire the knowledge, behaviors and skills taught in the program of study. The curriculum is designed to provide the general education necessary for the students selected for medicine. Students will learn the fundamental principles, develop critical judgment and apply principles and skills wisely in solving scientific and health related problems. Curricular goals and/or minimal graduation requirements have been developed to fulfill these objectives and to prepare graduates to pursue further education, if desired.

Our application process and steps to applying for aid can be found on https://www.downstate.edu/education-training/student-services/financial-aid/index.html

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Admissions Committee seeks applicants who have demonstrated, through their experiences that they have a motivation for service to others and their communities and to underserved populations. While preference is given to New York State applicants, well qualified out-of-state applicants are also considered. In addition, the Admission Committee seeks applicants from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, applicants who are first-generation college graduates, or applicants who have served in the military.  We employ a holistic review of the applicant pool and consider the following factors in our selection process: Academic metrics, Unusual features in the academic record, Study habits and work history, Communication skills, experience with small group learning modalities, Life experiences beyond the traditional pre-medical activities.  

Visit for additional information: https://www.downstate.edu/education-training/college-of-medicine/admissions/policies/index.html
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants must be able to demonstrate an understanding of the clinical aspects and passion for a career in medicine.
